Photo geotagging without a track file

No GPX? Use nearby iPhone photos as location clues.

iPhone photos from the same outing can place camera photos between known times and locations. Every result stays a reviewable suggestion—not recovered GPS.

How the no-GPX method works

Build a location timeline from photos you already took.

  1. Find eligible iPhone anchorsOnly geotagged photos identified as iPhone photos become evidence.
  2. Compare the nearest timesLensPin looks before and after each adjusted camera capture time.
  3. Check time and distanceNearby anchors support one another; distant anchors indicate movement.
  4. Review the suggested pointInspect both anchors, time gaps, map and explanation before selecting it.

What makes evidence stronger

Close in time, close in place, visible on both sides.

Before and after

Two-sided evidence explains the interval better than one anchor.

↔

Locations agree

Anchors in the same small area suggest you stayed nearby.

5m

Short time gaps

Minutes are easier to trust than hours; the chosen maximum remains a hard limit.

When the timeline shows movement

LensPin does not draw a straight line between distant photos.

If two anchors are more than 300 metres apart, LensPin favors the nearer time instead of inventing the route between them. The result is downgraded for review.

Nearby anchors

Same-area evidence

  • Use the shared area as the suggestion
  • Give more weight to short time gaps
Distant anchors

Movement evidence

  • Favor the nearer time with lower confidence
  • Give no suggestion when it is too far away

Only one nearby iPhone photo?

A one-sided clue can help, but it needs more caution.

One close-in-time anchor can help, but without a second photo it receives a penalty and may land in Review. A 10:02 anchor can support a 10:07 photo far better than an 11:30 photo.

Matching happens on the device.

Photos are not uploaded, and only identified iPhone photos become anchors. Read the privacy details →

Inside the no-GPX review

See what nearby iPhone photos can—and cannot—support.

LensPin keeps both nearby iPhone photos visible so you can tell whether the suggestion represents a stable place, movement, or only a weak one-sided clue.

See the actual anchors

Before-and-after thumbnails, capture times, time gaps, and map positions stay attached to the camera photo.

Understand movement

Nearby anchors can support a shared area. Distant anchors are treated as movement, not as permission to invent a route between them.

Open No suggestion too

The detail view shows the nearest eligible iPhone photos and which time or distance limit they failed.
